original_question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for causing Keratitis–ichthyosis–deafness (KID) syndrome located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for causing Keratitis–ichthyosis–deafness (KID) syndrome located?
final_qi.long_answer: Keratitis–ichthyosis–deafness (KID) syndrome is most often caused by missense mutations in the GJB2 gene, which encodes the gap-junction protein connexin 26. GJB2 is mapped to the long arm of chromosome 13 (13q11-q12). Pathogenic variants at this locus disrupt intercellular communication in epidermal and cochlear tissues, producing the triad of keratitis, skin ichthyosis-like changes, and sensorineural deafness characteristic of KID syndrome.
